object: Black granite statue of Isis seated nursing Horus; 17-line inscription on the back pilaster
site: Napata (Gebel Barkal or Merawi: the squeeze is marked Barkal, L., D. gives Merawi); now Berlin Inv. 2258
notes: Berlin Inv. 2258; published L., D. VI, Bl. 7, no. 28 (Pls. II, III). Griffith: 'archaic form of character'; the text may describe Isis (named four times). His line notes: l. 1 aleqese ('Aleqes', perhaps 'belonging to Aleq' = Philae?), its first a clear on Lepsius's squeeze but worn on the original; in eqeter the q is cut in a hollow and the final r, now lost, is clear on the squeeze; ater 'in composition' in ll. 2 and 7, so atere is joined across Griffith's type-line break; l. 3 teñkel, 'Can Dunqula (Dongola) be connected with it?' (teñkel is also joined across the type-line break in l. 10/11); l. 8 'the letters ep are quite clear'; l. 10 weyi, 'or with m, Meyi'; l. 11 compare the title te-n-se; tno(12)kedd 'probably a proper name' (Tanêkizaz), sr(13)be 'occurs elsewhere', both joined across his superscripts as in his notes; l. 14 'se ñ might be read' for te-se; l. 16 woSqol is 'Wêsh-qêl' (cf. 76); l. 17 nbto 'or noto'. Griffith also prints '?' over the divider before weyi and over the hatched lost signs at the end of l. 6 and before woSqol (both kept as [.]). p and k told apart by the top (rounded ε = p, flat Z = k).
